notes: §1985:XVI.1.4.3 GRL2.1: an independent segment is in its last-used state when "Control is transferred implicitly to that segment from a segment with a different segment-number"; §1985:IV.4.4.2 GR1 makes the return from a PERFORM/USE/SORT range and every iterative re-entry of a PERFORM range implicit. AlterSwitchEmitter.EmitSegmentState emits __seg and __EnterSegment (the reset of the segment's alterable GO TOs); DispatchEmitter.EmitDispatchMethod resets only on a pc whose segment differs from __seg, restores the caller's __seg in a finally on every nested dispatch return (PERFORM, __RunUse, __RunDebug, SORT procedure), and on __lastUsed enters the range's segment without reset; ControlFlowEmitter.EmitOutOfLinePerform/DispatchCall pass the per-execution __segIter flag so iteration 2+ is last-used (PB5380 landed). Witness: PERFORM F1 from seg 50 returns, GO TO I0 takes the ALTER. Probes at 85 (work-rs-13): (a) VARYING bounded by an ODO count INITIAL 1, ALTERED 2, 3; (b/c) 0 TIMES literal COBOL2386, cross-segment ALTER and PERFORM THRU 60/70 COBOL6877, EXIT PARAGRAPH COBOL0900, segment-numbers COBOL0902 and ALTER COBOL0810 at 2002/2014/2023; (d) n/a (control-flow rule, no operand class); (e) USE return after failed OPEN of SEQUENTIAL, INDEXED and RELATIVE files (FS=35), SORT INPUT PROCEDURE return, USE FOR DEBUGGING section return: each next GO TO took the ALTERed target, explicit GO TO back from seg 0 INITIAL; (f) 3 TIMES, UNTIL, VARYING..AFTER, TEST AFTER, PIC 9(18) count: INITIAL then ALTERED; zero and negative variable counts run nothing; VARYING whose range adds to its own variable INITIAL +01, ALTERED +03, +05; two separate PERFORM statements each INITIAL.
